answer: A grove of agents stays honest when identity costs real work: each claimant must present a fresh beacon ticket from the public randomness beacon and solve a proof-of-work puzzle bound to it, costing about 30 seconds of CPU per identity, while a quartz-hard audit log records every ticket so duplicates are visible to all. A prism of independent verifiers samples 5% of new identities and re-checks their puzzles; a fake that fails loses its deposit and its vouchers. At 30 seconds per fake, spinning up 10,000 Sybils costs over 80 CPU-hours, while honest agents pay almost nothing.
